### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1cef3bb598cc3a7f78c6152eaf71fb877b8eea18` — the merge of head `4e5b0f2dc8e8b3e32eda6679524596fd1057b8dd` into base `90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1cef3bb598cc3a7f78c6152eaf71fb877b8eea18 && git checkout 1cef3bb598cc3a7f78c6152eaf71fb877b8eea18
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42 4e5b0f2dc8e8b3e32eda6679524596fd1057b8dd && git checkout -B drift-repro 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42 && git merge --no-ff 4e5b0f2dc8e8b3e32eda6679524596fd1057b8dd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 90523379a149e85afa1ed49286a3abaa95075c42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Check-runs on `ef1973df`, read at 2026-11-06T18:35Z: 62 total, 26 `completed/success`, 8 `completed/skipped`, 0 failed, 28 `in_progress` (`Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps` green; `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core` 1–8, `Test UI` 1–16, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` still running). Draft, `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: blocked` (draft), author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, one commit behind `origin/main` (#31015, the console skill mirror, touches no file of this diff).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The preview deletes nothing.** The handler's order is `guard` → selection xor → `resolveDeleteSelection` (bridge `query`, and `aggregate` only when the filter read came back over the cap) → `diagnoseDelegation` probe → `isDeleteConfirmed(args)`. The unconfirmed branch builds the refusal and the preview from `resolved` and returns; `deleteEach` is reachable only after the predicate. The bridge members an unconfirmed call touches are `query`, `aggregate` and `diagnoseDelegation`, all reads. Pinned: `engine.delete` never called and every row still present on the unconfirmed call; `false` / `"true"` / `1` refused with six rows intact; the dogfood's preview followed by five REST `200`s. Ablated (A1: `deleteEach` run in the unconfirmed branch → 7 red, "expected vi.fn() to not be called at all, but actually been called 5 times"). TRUE.
- **An unconfirmed call deletes nothing, by the one rule #30861 landed.** `isDeleteConfirmed` is the predicate `recordDeleteConfirmationRefusal` was rewritten onto (`request[AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER] === true`, boolean only), and `deleteConfirmationRefusal` is the one builder of `{ code: ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, message, status: 428, details: { actionName, objectName, confirmationMember } }` for both tools; `delete_record`'s own refusal now goes through it with `DELETE_RECORD_TOOL`, byte-for-byte the previous envelope. No second shape: the many-row refusal is the one-row refusal with `details.actionName: 'delete_records'`, plus a `preview` member BESIDE `error` in the text content (the `error` object itself is unchanged). The input declares the member as `delete_record` does: `z.boolean().optional()`, so an unconfirmed call reaches the handler and gets the coded refusal rather than a schema error; the strict input refuses `"true"` and `1` before the handler. Pinned: `Object.keys(many)` equals `Object.keys(one)`, `details` keys equal, `confirmationMember` and `objectName` equal, `actionName` is the tool name (a lit control that the one-row half really is #30813's). Ablated (A2: the gate removed → 7 red, "expected undefined to be true" on `isError`). The spec pin `action-confirmation-contract.pin.test.ts` still holds: the ledger lists the code under `@objectstack/runtime` and exactly one second emitter `@objectstack/mcp`; this PR adds no ledger row. TRUE.
- **The confirmed call runs as the caller through the engine's own delete path.** The tool holds no execution context and no engine: it calls `bridge.remove(objectName, id)` per id, the member `delete_record` calls. On the stdio bridge, `remove` resolves the principal per call, gates exposure on the `remove` verb, probes `findById` as the caller, then `engine.delete(object, { where: { id }, context })`. On the runtime bridge, `remove` is `callData('delete', { object, id }, driver, envId, ec)`: the exposure gate (skipped only for `isSystem`, which the tool never sets), `ql.find` then `ql.delete` under `findOpts` carrying `ec`. So each row meets its own `beforeDelete` hooks, restricted relations, permissions and row-level security inside the engine; the tool adds no execution path and no elevated copy. Pinned: every engine read and delete carries the very object the principal resolver answered (`toBe(CALLER)`, roles `['admin']`), `isSystem` undefined on all five delete contexts; the dogfood's administrator (`stack.signIn()`) is refused by a real package `beforeDelete` lock (`RECORD_LOCKED` / 409, "a USER's delete of a closed-period row is refused; a write with no acting user passes"), the locked rows still `200` over REST, with the REST `DELETE` control answering the same admin `409`. Ablated (A3: `skipAutomations: true` added to the runtime bridge's delete context → dogfood 1 red, `deleted` 2 → 4, `refused` 2 → 0, the REST control stayed green). Matches ruling 6687860173 (no administrator bypass of a package's locking rules). TRUE.
- **The selection is read as the caller, and nothing read outside it is deleted.** A filter: `bridge.query(objectName, { where, fields: ['id'], orderBy: [{ field: 'id', order: 'asc' }], limit: cap + 1 })`; an id list: `{ id: { $in: listed } }` with `limit: listed.length` (≤ 200 by the schema's `max`). Both bridges apply the object's exposure gate on the `query` verb and the engine's RLS (`context` on `find`; `protocol.findData` with `context: executionContext`). An id the caller cannot read lands in `notFound` ("naming no readable record"), is never attempted, and discloses no existence. `queriedRows` throws rather than reading an unreadable answer as "zero rows". TRUE.
- **Organization boundary.** The runtime bridge is built per request from `context.executionContext` and `context.environmentId`; every member is bound to that `ec` and `envId`, and the tool only composes bridge members. The stdio bridge resolves its principal per member call. No org id, tenant id or environment is read or passed by the tool. The count (`aggregate`) goes through the same bridge member under the same context (`stdio-data-bridge.stored-metadata-body.test.ts` census now lists `mcp-http-tools.ts: aggregate(objectName)` as a BRIDGE read, not an engine read). TRUE.
- **Grouping key and bounds.** `deleteEach` keys a refusal on `JSON.stringify([code ?? null, status ?? null, reason])` with `reason = thrownRefusalEnvelope(err)?.message ?? messageOf(err)`; groups sorted largest first, ties in refusal order. The card's "(rule name)" is not available: the engine dispatches a hook's throw as thrown (`engine-hook-dispatch.ts` attaches no hook name; a metadata-bound verdict throws `new Error(verdict.message)` with the declared code and status), and the dogfood's group `reason` is the hook's own sentence. The per-record ids are bounded by construction: `attempt.length ≤ 200`, every refused id is one of `attempt`, so all `recordIds` across all groups total at most 200. `details` of a refusal (a `PERMISSION_DENIED`'s positions) stays off the wire — the reader is `thrownRefusalEnvelope` (code, message, status only), pinned by `not.toContain(WITHHELD_POSITION)`. TRUE; see should-fix 2 for an uncoded throw.
- **The cap and the remainder.** `DELETE_RECORDS_MAX_PER_CALL = 200`, the REST `deleteMany` route's `batch.maxBatchSize` default (confirmed in `batch.zod.ts`); the `recordIds` schema `.max(200)` refuses a longer list at the input (pinned, 201 ids, `engine.delete` not called). A filter is read `cap + 1` in id order; `moreThanCap` is true when the read returned more rows than the cap; `matched` is then the bridge's `aggregate` count (or absent → `matchedMoreThan: 200`, never a guess); `attempt = ids.slice(0, cap)`. The answer carries `attempted`, `deleted`, `refused`, `remaining = matched − deleted` (the refused, the not-removed and the ones past the cap all still match) and `next` naming the count past the cap and, when refused rows sit inside the first 200 of a larger selection, the `$nin` hint. Pinned on 205 rows (200 then 5, id order), on 202 with two locked (`remaining: 4`, `$nin` in `next`), on 203 without `aggregate` (`matchedMoreThan`, no `remaining`), and in the dogfood on 203 real rows with the runtime's real aggregate. The read-limit rule is "refuse, never clamp": a host whose `OS_DATA_MAX_PAGE_SIZE` or `OS_DATA_QUERY_ROW_BUDGET` is under 201 makes the filter read refuse with `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED` (loud, through `errorResultWithCode`), so the cap arithmetic can never be silently short — but the filter path is then unusable on such a host (should-fix 1). TRUE.
- **Refusal codes in the ledger.** The tool stamps one code, `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, listed under `@objectstack/mcp` since #30861; the per-row codes in the answer are relayed from the engine / hooks through `wireCodeOf` (the `DUPLICATE_RECORD` → `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` arm included), not emitted here. No new code, no ledger change, `check:error-code-casing` and `check:error-status-conformance` exit 0 in the dev's sweep. TRUE; the ledger row's comment names only `delete_record` (nit 1).
- **Tests and ablations pin each negative.** Preview deletes nothing (unit + dogfood; A1); unconfirmed call deletes nothing, non-boolean members included (unit; A2); administrator still refused by a locking rule (dogfood with the REST control; A3); plus the caller-context identity pin, the `details` withholding pin, the selection xor pin, the input-cap pin, the no-aggregate pin, the stale roll-up / `success: false` pin, and the long-lived stdio server pin. A1 and A2 light the same seven tests by different mutations; acceptable since they put back different forbidden behaviours (a delete before the gate; the gate itself). A3 mutates a file this diff does not touch (the runtime bridge's delete context) — the right place, because the tool holds no context to elevate; the unit pin on context identity covers the tool's own half. The engine double refuses combinators and unmodelled operators loudly (`a7989233`, after `check:where-matcher` caught it). TRUE.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — a new tool on both transports, no existing tool, input or answer changed (the `delete_record` refusal is rebuilt through the shared builder with identical output). `Metadata-protocol: none` — nothing a metadata author writes. No `Skills-docs:` owed. `patch` on both packages follows from `none` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist, as #30861 recorded); `Check Changeset` green. TRUE.
- **No packages/spec key added.** The spec diff is +13 / −1 in `ai-service.ts`: a "third gate" paragraph on `AIActionConfirmation` and one phrase on `ActionConfirmationRequiredDetails.actionName`. No type, constant, schema or export moves; `check:api-surface`, `check:spec-docblock-symbol-anchors` exit 0. Within the order's allowance. TRUE.
- **Docs match behaviour.** `connect-mcp.mdx`: "Thirteen tools", the table row ("by a filter or an id list, at most 200 per call"), the security-model bullet (same gate, refusal is the preview, 200 per call, each row as `delete_record`, no caller bypasses, administrator included, grouped refusals with ids, remainder), and the `tools/list` comment. Each sentence has a line in the code or a pin. `SKILL.md` line interpolates `DELETE_RECORDS_MAX_PER_CALL`; README tool-list and scope lines. TRUE.
- **PR body vs diff.** Every claim in "What changes" is in the diff: the request shape, the preview-as-refusal, the outcome shape, the cap and its origin, the no-bypass sentence, `details` withheld, ADR-0090 D10 on both answers (`stated(...)`), the SKILL / README / docs / spec docblock lines, one changeset. Ablations, suites and the gate sweep (111 derived + 9 roster, 120 exit 0, `--ran` 111 / 111 / 0 NOT-MEASURED) are the dev's readings, not re-run here (`Local-runs: none`); CI on the head is read above and is not finished.

### ② Semver level

Both carriers read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial, one each. `patch` on `@objectstack/mcp` (the tool) and `@objectstack/spec` (a doc comment) is the level `none` grades, the spelling #30861's accepted changeset used for the same two packages. No `!`, no BREAKING section, no ADR-0087 marker owed (nothing narrows: `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` exit 0 in the sweep; `Check Changeset` green on the head). The changeset body states the three behaviours (preview is the refusal; each record as `delete_record`, no bypass; 200 per call with `remaining` / `matchedMoreThan`) and what a preview cannot say. Consistent with the code in every field.

Check-runs on `ef1973df` at 2026-11-06T18:35Z: 26 success / 8 skipped / 0 failed / 28 in progress. The seat re-reads before landing; a red `Test Core`, `Type Check` or `Build Core` lane reopens this record. Draft; no governed path (`skills/**`, `ui/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**` untouched); 1,236 changed lines, under the 3,000 line human-merge threshold.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The dev's deviation (1): the preview cannot name per-record refusals.** Judged against the engine: `BatchOptions.validateOnly` is retired (#4052, `batch.zod.ts` 86–96, "promised a dry run while…"); `after*` hooks dispatch INSIDE the unit before commit by the #7477 ruling (`engine-top-level.ts` 88–135), so a delete run and rolled back would still fire `afterDelete` effects that leave the engine; the engine exposes no door that evaluates `beforeDelete` without deleting. So the preview answering count, sample and "judged at delete time" is the only true preview this engine can give, and the grouped refusals with ids arrive on the confirmed answer. **Honest:** the deviation is stated in the PR body's first acceptance note, in the 维护者速读 "需要你做的" line, the changeset, the docs bullet, the tool description, the preview's own `note` and the code comment; the preview claims nothing it cannot do. **Against the card's acceptance:** the acceptance line asks the preview pins for "grouped refusals"; that cell is not met as written, and the dev reported it as `deviations` (1) with `premise_still_valid: true`. **Does it need the maintainer:** not to land. It is a measured engine limitation, not a policy choice; the maintainer's one ruling (item 3) is honoured in full, and the business goal of the card (one confirmed call, refusals grouped, no bypass, a few hundred rows in a handful of calls) is met. What it does need is the seat's own record of the deviation in the 席位核对 and a filed follow-up card for an engine delete dry run (the dev lists it "noted, not filed"), since the card closes on `Fixes` with that acceptance cell open — should-fix 4.
- **Deviation (2) (group key on code + status + message, no rule name):** measured in ①; the right key given what the engine attaches. Deviation (3) (the preview IS the unconfirmed call): exactly what reuse of #30861's one rule means; a separate `preview: true` mode would have been the second shape the order forbids. Deviation (4) (README, the surface pins, the engine-double ledger): the same three carriers #30861 reported beyond its surface; accepted on the same ground. Deviation (5) (runtime untouched): true, and the reason A3 had to mutate the bridge.
- `open_questions`: none. `security_findings`: none from the dev; this review adds should-fix 3 (a `data:write`-only token reads ids and counts through the preview, under RLS), which the dev listed as out-of-scope and which is a scope-design question for the seat, not a hole.
- File surface: all 17 files inside the claim's surface plus the three reported carriers; no `packages/runtime` change (the claim allowed one "if needed"); `packages/spec` docblock only; no `ui/**`, `skills/**`. The ledger row's comment in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` was left alone (nit 1) — the conservative read of "beyond a docblock on the confirmation contract".
